data.title: The Hidden Costs of Remote Work
data.passage:
Remote work was once praised as a way to cut costs and improve work-life balance. However, as more companies adopt hybrid or fully remote arrangements, researchers are uncovering hidden drawbacks that affect both employees and employers. A 2023 study from the University of Chicago found that remote workers often struggle to sustain focus when home environments lack structure. The study tracked 1,200 employees over six months and revealed that those working from home reported higher levels of mental fatigue than their office-based counterparts. This fatigue, in turn, reduced their overall productivity by nearly 15 percent. The convenience of avoiding the daily commute, it seems, comes at a cognitive price.

One major issue is the blurring of boundaries between work and personal life. Without a clear separation, many remote workers find it difficult to disconnect, leading to longer hours and increased stress. In fact, the lack of a physical office removes the natural incentive to stop working at a reasonable hour. Some companies have tried to address this by offering a home-office subsidy, which covers part of the cost for ergonomic furniture or internet upgrades. But such financial support does little to solve the deeper problem of time management. What matters is not the money spent but the establishment of clear expectations and routines.

Another challenge is the allocation of resources and space. In crowded urban areas, where housing is expensive and space is limited, setting aside a dedicated workspace is often impossible. This leads to what experts call "space congestion"—a situation where work and living areas overlap, making it hard to concentrate. Yet, some resilient employees manage to adapt by creating makeshift offices in corners or using noise-canceling headphones. However, these individual solutions are not scalable; they depend on personal circumstances and cannot replace systematic support from employers.

Finally, the loss of face-to-face interaction can weaken team cohesion and informal learning. While digital tools enable communication, they cannot fully replicate the spontaneous conversations that spark innovation. In practice, companies that allocate time for virtual social events see only modest improvements in team bonding. It is not the frequency of meetings but the quality of connection that suffers. As organizations navigate this new landscape, they must weigh the benefits of flexibility against the hidden costs of isolation and fatigue—a balance that will shape the future of work.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Remote work offers more benefits than drawbacks for most employees.

options.label: B
options.text: The shift to remote work brings hidden costs that require careful consideration.

options.label: C
options.text: Companies should provide subsidies for home-office equipment.

options.label: D
options.text: Digital tools can fully replace face-to-face interaction in remote teams.

evidence.sentence: However, as more companies adopt hybrid or fully remote arrangements, researchers are uncovering hidden drawbacks that affect both employees and employers.

questions.explanation: 文章首段提出远程工作虽有好处，但存在隐藏缺陷，后续段落分别讨论专注力、边界模糊、空间拥挤和社交缺失等问题，B项概括全文。

distractorNotes.label: A
distractorNotes.note: 原文明确否定：首段指出隐藏缺陷，并非好处多于坏处。

distractorNotes.label: C
distractorNotes.note: 部分正确：第二段提到补贴，但只是细节，非全文主旨。

distractorNotes.label: D
distractorNotes.note: 原文明确否定：第四段指出数字工具不能完全替代面对面交流。

questions.stem: According to the 2023 University of Chicago study, what was found about remote workers?

options.label: A
options.text: They reported more mental fatigue than office workers.

options.label: B
options.text: They were more productive than office workers.

options.label: C
options.text: They had better work-life balance.

options.label: D
options.text: They spent less time on work.

evidence.sentence: The study tracked 1,200 employees over six months and revealed that those working from home reported higher levels of mental fatigue than their office-based counterparts.

questions.explanation: 原文明确提到居家办公者报告了更高水平的心理疲劳，A项是正确改写。

distractorNotes.label: B
distractorNotes.note: 原文明确否定：研究显示生产力下降15%。

distractorNotes.label: C
distractorNotes.note: 原文未提及：研究未比较工作与生活平衡。

distractorNotes.label: D
distractorNotes.note: 原文未提及：研究未测量工作时间。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the home-office subsidy?

options.label: A
options.text: It effectively solves the problem of time management.

options.label: B
options.text: It covers all costs for home-office equipment.

options.label: C
options.text: It fails to address the deeper issue of time management.

options.label: D
options.text: It is provided by all companies.

evidence.sentence: But such financial support does little to solve the deeper problem of time management.

questions.explanation: 原文明确说补贴对解决时间管理问题作用不大，C项正确。

distractorNotes.label: A
distractorNotes.note: 原文明确否定：补贴不能解决时间管理问题。

distractorNotes.label: B
distractorNotes.note: 过于绝对：原文说补贴只覆盖部分费用。

distractorNotes.label: D
distractorNotes.note: 过于绝对：原文说一些公司提供补贴，并非所有。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about individual solutions to space congestion?

options.label: A
options.text: They are sufficient for all employees.

options.label: B
options.text: They are not a long-term solution for companies.

options.label: C
options.text: They are supported by employers.

options.label: D
options.text: They increase productivity significantly.

evidence.sentence: However, these individual solutions are not scalable; they depend on personal circumstances and cannot replace systematic support from employers.

questions.explanation: 原文指出个人解决方案不可扩展且不能替代系统性支持，因此推断出它们不是公司的长期解决方案。

distractorNotes.label: A
distractorNotes.note: 过于绝对：原文说这些方案依赖个人情况，并非对所有人都足够。

distractorNotes.label: C
distractorNotes.note: 原文明确否定：原文说它们不能替代雇主的系统性支持。

distractorNotes.label: D

evidence.sentence: In fact, the lack of a physical office removes the natural incentive to stop working at a reasonable hour.

questions.explanation: incentive意为“激励、动机”，此处指缺乏促使按时停止工作的自然动机，A项正确。

distractorNotes.label: B
distractorNotes.note: 原文未提及：incentive不是经济处罚。

distractorNotes.label: C
distractorNotes.note: 原文未提及：incentive不是法律要求。

distractorNotes.label: D
distractorNotes.note: 部分正确：physical space是原文另一概念，与incentive无关。
